articles.title: Eduardinho dos Teclados: baiano viralizou com hit inspirado em Vini Jr | G1
articles.standfirst: Natural do distrito de Gabiarra, em Eunápolis, Eduardo Costa da Silva tem realizado apresentações em diversas cidades do Brasil após sucesso com o hit "Baile do VJ".
articles.summary: Natural de Eunápolis, no extremo sul da Bahia, Eduardo Costa da Silva tem realizado apresentações em diversas cidades do Brasil após sucesso com o hit "Baile do VJ".
articles.body:
O hit " Baile do VJ ", cuja letra é inspirada no atacante brasileiro Vinícius Júnior, viralizou nas redes sociais e mudou a carreira do artista baiano Eduardo Costa da Silva, de 31 anos. Conhecido como Eduardinho dos Teclados , o cantor, que é natural do distrito de Gabiarra, em Eunápolis , no extremo sul do estado, tem deficiência visual e precisou enfrentar o preconceito no início da carreira.

Em entrevista ao g1 , Eduardinho contou que nasceu com a deficiência visual e, em suas próprias palavras, seus ouvidos sempre foram seus olhos . Aos 5 anos, começou a tocar cavaquinho, mas foi a partir da adolescência que conheceu o teclado em uma igreja católica.

A partir desse encontro, o artista nunca mais se separou do instrumento. Com ajuda da prima, que o guiou por Eunápolis, ele chegou a fazer alguns dias de aulas de música, mas detalha que aprendeu a tocar quase completamente sozinho.

"Uma prima minha me localizou aqui na cidade para a gente fazer aula, curso de teclado. Fiquei 15 dias na aula, depois eu fui para casa e o resto aprendi tudo sozinho, escutando as pessoas".

Conheça Eduardinho dos Teclados, cantor baiano com deficiência visual que viralizou com música inspirada em Vinícius Júnior — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Ele começou a investir na carreira como músico aos 16 anos, com apresentações em bares, casamentos e serestas na região. Na época, o cantor performava canções de artistas como Pablo do Arrocha e Tayrone, acompanhado apenas do som do teclado.

Com o passar do tempo, ele buscou espaços maiores, mas recebeu muitas negativas de produtores de eventos.

"O que atrapalhou mesmo, que me deixou um pouco abalado num período, foi só a questão do preconceito. [...] As pessoas não acreditavam muito no meu trabalho por conta de não ter muita estrutura, era o começo do projeto e o pessoal não dava muita credibilidade".

Apesar do preconceito devido à falta de visão e inexperiência, ele afirma que sempre acreditou em seu futuro como artista.

"Desde meus 5 anos de idade, eu já acreditava que tinha capacidade de criar um projeto e seguir a minha carreira. A deficiência não atrapalhou, ela foi um incentivo".

Desde o sucesso de "Baile do VJ", que explodiu nas redes sociais, Eduardinho vem conquistando espaço em diferentes palcos do país e superando barreiras. A música é uma composição de Daniel Mendes, inspirada no atacante do Real Madrid, e representou a "virada de chave" na carreira do baiano.

A canção viralizou no início do ano e ganhou novo fôlego com a atuação do jogador pela Seleção Brasileira durante a Copa do Mundo de 2026 . Eduardinho sempre escutou muito futebol e, apesar de não conhecer o atleta pessoalmente, passou a sentir um vínculo com ele.

"Se eu conhecesse ele um dia, seria muito maravilhoso. Porque a música, querendo ou não, tem a ver com ele. Acho que ele já deve ter visto essa, fez até a dancinha", brinca.

Acessibilidade nos palcos e relação com o público

Eduardinho destacou que a relação com a banda e outros membros de sua equipe é essencial neste período de adaptação à rotina extensa de apresentações. Com uma média de 30 shows mensais, o artista conta com a ajuda dos colegas para uma melhor adaptação durante as performances ao vivo.

Nos últimos meses, o baiano passou por estados como Tocantins, Alagoas, Pará e Minas Gerais. Além da passagem de som e checagem de equipamentos, os membros da equipe ajudam o cantor a se localizar no ambiente ao realizar uma espécie de "mapeamento" do palco.

Entretanto, o verdadeiro guia do cantor é o clamor do público. Ele conta que a reação das pessoas com a apresentação é perceptível e, quanto mais animado, mais ele se entrega à apresentação.

"Dá para perceber quando a galera está animada. Quando a galera está bem animada, aí você vai para cima com tudo", ressalta.

O artista acrescentou ainda que a relação com a plateia sempre foi um destaque em sua carreira. Quando começou, durante um show no São João de Eunápolis, ele chegou a se apresentar para mais de 7 mil pessoas. Em outros momentos, performou para uma plateia vazia.

Esses altos e baixos da carreira não assustam o baiano. Com planos para gravar um DVD e tocando o projeto "Baile do Eduardinho", o cantor diz estar focado em aproveitar as oportunidades que têm surgido.

"Agora a gente tem uns 'feats' para fazer, então estou deixando rolar", simplifica.

articles.title: Newspaper headlines: 'Noel's crying his heart out' and 'global IVF disaster'
articles.summary: A couple of the papers feature more reaction to the Manchester City drama, after the club was found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules.
articles.body:
Many of Sunday's newspapers look ahead to Andy Burnham's first Labour conference as prime minister.

The Observer describes him as a "people-pleaser with a ruthless streak of ambition." "A skilled communicator praised for his ordinariness," it argues, "will need to bring more clarity to his vision."

"Buoyant Burnham is more popular than his party," according to the Sunday Express . The Sunday Mirror says that losing his father has fuelled his social care mission. The family heartache has spurred him to "grasp the nettle" of reform, it says.

The Sunday Times writes that ahead of the conference, Chancellor John Healey has raised hopes of help on fuel duty in next month's Budget. The Mail on Sunday believes Labour is at war over migrants and the economy, with cabinet ministers trading blows on the eve of the conference.

The Sunday Telegraph says Burnham is already out of ideas. The country does not need more speeches about "hope," it argues - it needs a prime minister willing to spend political capital forcing change through, whatever the objections of Labour MPs.

The Sunday Times says an estimated 800,000 people greeted the Pope as he travelled down the Champs Elysees in Paris on Sunday. It titles a photo of his visit "Mass appeal." The Sun on Sunday headlines its coverage "Chateauneuf-du-Pope."

"They think it's all over... it's not" says the Sunday Mirror , as it considers the Manchester City's chairman's insistence that - as the Sunday Express puts it, the club's "not guilty" of breaching the Premier League's financial rules. The Sunday People says one of the club's most famous fans, Noel Gallagher, has insisted the crisis is nothing to do with the players or supporters. The Daily Star Sunday reaches for not one, but two Oasis song titles for its coverage. Noel's crying his heart out, it says on page one - while on the back page, suggesting the club chairman is urging people to "Stand by me."

The Sunday Times says it can finally answer the divisive question of whether you need to rinse cans and jars before recycling them - something, the paper says, has caused marriages to crumble.

The head of Britain's biggest recycling firm, Veolia, has told the paper there's no need to rise them out as long as they are "relatively clean." Divorce rates will fall, delights the paper. Except for one nagging question: "What exactly do you mean when you say "relatively."

images.caption: The Premier League drama, after Manchester City was found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules, features again on the front page of some of Sunday's papers. Oasis's Noel Gallagher is "crying his heart out" over the news, the Daily Star reports, as the musician says he is "sad for City fans"

articles.title: 'Old-Fashioned Butt Whooping,' Ole Miss HC Pete Golding Sounds Off on Loss to No. 21 Florida
articles.summary: Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding wasn't exactly thrilled with the No. 4 Rebels' 52-28 defeat at the hands of No. 21 Florida on Saturday.
articles.body:
Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding wasn't exactly thrilled with the No. 4 Rebels' 52-28 defeat at the hands of No. 21 Florida on Saturday.

Golding called the loss an "old-fashioned butt whooping" while also wondering if he had enough players with a "burning in your gut" to fix the problems that plagued them, per ESPN's Andrea Adelson .

Ole Miss trailed 17-6 at halftime against Florida before the Gators scored 35 points in the second half to wrap up the lopsided victory.

Expert CFB Locks for Week 4's Biggest Games 🔒

Golding's defense struggled throughout the contest, giving up 498 total yards. The Gators also picked up 302 rushing yards as a team, averaging 5.7 yards per attempt.

The Rebels amassed 426 total yards of their own, although they couldn't keep up with Florida's offense. Ole Miss finished with two turnovers while converting just four of 11 opportunities on third down.

Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss went 25-of-34 for 298 yards and one touchdown compared to one interception. Chambliss scored twice on the ground as well.

"I don't want them to get this taste out of their mouth," Golding said, per Adelson. "That's what I told them. I never got the taste out of my mouth from Miami walking off the field [in last year's CFP semifinal loss]. Part of the problem sometimes is we move on too fast. The sun's going to come up tomorrow and it's a new day, but it's a new day to go get better at what we don't do well."

The loss was particularly disappointing considering Ole Miss entered the contest with plenty of momentum, scoring 82 combined points in wins over Louisville and Charlotte to open the season before making a statement with a 32-24 victory against LSU on Sept. 19.

Golding's squad will attempt to get back on track in its next game, a matchup with Vanderbilt on Oct. 10.

articles.title: No. 10 LSU bounces back from Ole Miss loss with dominant 29-point win over No. 23 Texas A&M
articles.summary: Quarterback Sam Leavitt played through an ankle injury, and finished with two touchdowns.
articles.body:
No. 10 LSU lost its first game under new head coach Lane Kiffin last week to Ole Miss , and this was the first chance for the Tigers to show how they would respond.

LSU took control early, scoring two first-half touchdowns and holding the Aggies to just three points. It looked like it would be a grueling game, but the Tigers came out of the half and dominated every phase. When the dust settled, LSU had earned the 35-6 blowout victory.

Although it came just four minutes into the second half, the game appeared mentally over for Texas A&M . LSU forced a three-and-out and then quarterback Sam Leavitt faked a run and flipped a pass to Jackson Harris , completely fooling the defense for the 57-yard score.

After the score, Texas A&M turned the ball over on downs. LSU then responded with another touchdown, and the Aggies never found a successful rhythm. No offensive drive lasted more than six plays for the remainder of the game.

LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt was dealing with an ankle injury throughout the game. He wasn't able to run much, but fought through the injury. The quarterback left the game twice when the Tigers got to the goal line, and backup quarterback Landen Clark punched in two rushing touchdowns. Leavitt also got to sit for most of the fourth quarter as Clark got more reps.

Kiffin wasn't satisfied with the blowout win. On the other side of the two-minute timeout, even up 29, Kiffin continued to call plays and move the offense down the field, despite being able to kneel out the clock. The Tigers would have scored another touchdown if their wide receiver Jayce Brown hadn't dropped a pass from Clark.

After the game, Kiffin called it "a really good rebound, from obviously, the devastation of last week of letting go of that game we felt we could've won. It was good to come back and get a win."

Kiffin clarified after the game that last week's loss to Ole Miss wasn't their Super Bowl, just the Rebels'. He praised his team for their ability to respond this week.

The Aggies couldn't get anything going on offense. Rueben Owens II ran the ball efficiently, picking up 62 yards on 11 carries. Unfortunately, the game script took the ball out of his hands.

Quarterback Marcel Reed had one of the worst games of his career, finishing 10-of-26 for 106 yards, no touchdowns, and an interception. It was the fewest amount of yards he had in a game in which he attempted at least 12 passes.

Reed had to start forcing passes to get the offense moving, but he threw an interception in the fourth quarter. The QB was trying to hit a receiver on the sideline or throw it away, but a Tigers DB jumped the route, and LSU was already in the red zone. The Tigers scored, increasing their lead to 29 and putting the final nail in the coffin.

Texas A&M began the season ranked eighth. With 2-2 record through four games, the Aggies will fall out of the Top 25 in the next AP poll. Texas A&M will look to bounce back next week at home against Arkansas after back-to-back conference losses.

LSU's loss to Ole Miss dropped the Tigers down to No. 10 this week. After taking on three Power Four teams in the first five weeks of the season, LSU will face McNeese next weekend in a game where Leavitt can hopefully get extra rest and heal up before a seven-game SEC slate to end the season.

articles.title: Yahoo Top 10: After beatdown of Ole Miss, just how good is Florida?
articles.summary: On a wild day of upsets and marquee matchups, the Gators flexed hardest with a dominant win over the Rebels at home. Who else made our Top 10 after a pivotal...
articles.body:
Last December, Florida athletic director Scott Stricklin did more than just kick the proverbial Lane Kiffin tires.

But when it was clear that he'd be headed to Baton Rouge, Stricklin turned to, at that point, a little-known former Kentucky linebacker who'd led Troy and Tulane to successful seasons. Nine months later, Jon Sumrall's Gators are the toast of college football after a drubbing of the Ole Miss Rebels on Saturday . Florida's ability to control the line of scrimmage and move the ball on the ground may present serious problems for the rest of the league.

Despite a 24-point win over a top-five team Saturday, Sumrall quipped to reporters afterward, "We have not arrived."

No, Jon, you have. Florida vaults into our Top 10 at No. 3.

Plenty other wildness transpired on the fourth full Saturday of college football. In the Big Ten, for instance, Iowa (over Michigan) and Wisconsin (over Penn State) picked up comeback wins on the road, and Oregon gashed through USC's defense even without starting quarterback Dante Moore . In the SEC, the Longhorns remain our top-ranked squad after beating Tennessee, Alabama QB Keelon Russell seems like the real deal and OU's Brent Venables owes the Sooners back that contract extension. If you're wondering why more than half of our Top 10 is from the SEC, look at the non-conference power league records (the SEC was the only power conference with a winning record — 10-2 — against the others over the first three weeks).

In the Big 12, Utah cracked our Top 10. In fact, are the Utes the best of the Big 12? They've certainly played the toughest schedule yet of the challengers in the conference. With a win at Louisville, Wake Forest made it more difficult to answer a vexing question: Who the heck will challenge Miami in the ACC?

Let's hit the rankings, which, no, don't yet include Indiana (wins over North Texas, Howard, Western Kentucky and Northwestern don't get you ranked).

No program in the country has the combination of two wins like Texas: Ohio State and at Tennessee. The Longhorns tried to cough it up late in Neyland Stadium, but they hung on to give QB Arch Manning a win at a special place (he wears jersey No. 16 because of uncle Peyton 's years in Knoxville). In an odd stat, Arch was sacked more times (6) than he threw incompletions (five). His 18-yard, third-down strike to Ryan Wingo on Texas' eight-play, 60-yard touchdown drive helped Steve Sarkisian's guys take a 10-point lead.

Last week, the Heisman Trophy seemed destined to head to Oxford and into the hands of QB Trinidad Chambliss. This week, it feels like it's right back to where it was originally: in Columbus in the glue-coated hands of Jeremiah Smith. The Buckeyes receiver and future NFL top-10 pick continued a heater of a season with 217 yards, 12 catches and four touchdowns on Saturday. He's up to more than 600 yards through four games and seven scores. He's a magician with his hands, catching nearly everything within a 2-mile radius.

Shocked? Don't be. The Gators have two wins in very impressive ways, scoring 44 points in a win at Auburn and then 52 against Ole Miss in The Swamp. First-year coach Jon Sumrall's team plays a physical brand of football that's fun to watch. They've rushed for nearly 550 yards in consecutive SEC games. That's no easy task. QB Aaron Philo is playing smart, consistent football and the Gators look like legit contenders in the league.

QB Darian Mensah's numbers through his first four games are simply absurd. Get this: He's got 12 incompletions — twelve! — and 14 touchdowns. Don't ignore that he's thrown for at least 330 yards twice, too. His favorite target, Malachi Toney (Baby Jesus!) caught another six passes for 120 yards on Saturday. The Hurricanes are as explosive as they've been the last few years. Can they continue the onslaught against a Clemson team that's, sort of, found some momentum?

Perhaps it's time to start talking about QB Keelon Russell in relation to the Heisman Trophy, no? He's completing more than 70 percent of his passes, has eight touchdowns and two picks. On Saturday against the Gamecocks, Russell misfired on just six passes and threw four touchdowns. He's got plenty of pieces around him too. Kane Wommack's defense held South Carolina to a 21 percent clip on third downs.

The Rebels need the bye next week. After an emotional victory against former coach Lane Kiffin and LSU, they laid the egg in Gainesville without star running back Kewan Lacy. The Gators' defense swallowed Ole Miss' ground attack and pressured Trinidad Chambliss just enough. But the most concerning thing for Pete Golding is his defense, which was exploited earlier this year against Louisville, nearly collapsed in the second half against LSU and allowed almost 500 yards on Saturday.

The Irish's schedule isn't glamorous so far. In fact, they haven't beaten a team that will finish ranked inside the top 25 at the end of the season (at least that's our assumption about Wisconsin, Rice, Michigan State and Purdue). But the wins are fairly dominant and despite the struggles at times to run the football, Marcus Freeman's defense is one salty group. They entered third in the country in total D — a ranking that won't move much after Purdue's 218 yards.

The Bulldogs haven't played the toughest schedule so far, which is why they're at No. 8. But between QB Gunner Stockton and Kirby Smart's defense, they appear to be legitimate SEC title contenders — again. On Saturday, they forced the Sooners into a plethora of mistakes, including two fumbles, an interception and a turnover on downs. It's no fun playing against the Dawgs defense, despite NIL and the portal making it more difficult for them to stockpile front-seven depth.

Get ready to hear a whole lot about a Mississippi kid named Kamario Taylor, the Bulldogs' electric sophomore starting quarterback. He's slung 14 touchdowns and just two picks and, most recently on Saturday, put up 360 yards passing against Missouri in State's first top-25 win in more than a decade. Are the Bulldogs perfect? No. The defense can be exploited but former head coach Zach Arnett, the defensive coordinator, has the unit playing good enough.

Welcome to the Top 10, Utes! They nearly let a 17-point lead slip away, but QB Devon Dampier showed just how slippery he can be. Most folks thought Dampier might follow Kyle Whittingham to Ann Arbor. Not so fast! He stuck around with new coach Morgan Scalley, who's got Utah playing its always-dependable D. On Saturday, RB Wayshawn Parker had a breakout performance (18 carries for 174 yards and three total TDs).

articles.title: College football winners and losers: How the SEC stacks up after a pivotal Week 4
articles.summary: Georgia looks to be the league's top team through the first four weeks of the season.
articles.body:
The SEC was the main character of the biggest Saturday of the 2026 season so far.

Four of the six matchups between teams ranked in the AP Top 25 were between SEC teams. And after Week 4, we have a pretty good idea of how the conference stacks up. Here's how we see what we think is the deepest league in college football.

The Bulldogs are ahead of the Longhorns here for a reason. They are the most dominant team in the SEC. And possibly even the country. Georgia beat Oklahoma 41-13 on Saturday to move to 4-0 and 2-0 in conference play. The 28-point win is Georgia's closest game of the season, though QB Gunner Stockton now finally does have more incompletions than passing TDs after he was 14-of-25 for 171 yards and just one touchdown.

The Longhorns got out of Knoxville, Tennessee, with a 20-17 win after the Vols converted an onside kick that may or may not have been legal . The two teams don't meet in the regular season, but might be on a collision course for the SEC title game.

Unless Alabama has something to say about it, that is. The Crimson Tide dominated South Carolina in a 49-18 win as Keelon Russell threw for 365 yards and four touchdowns. Russell has become an immediate star in his first season as a starter and WR Ryan Coleman-Williams had five catches for 98 yards and two touchdowns. The Tide host Georgia in two weeks.

It's early, but ascending to favorite status

The Gators are going to be much higher in the AP Top 25 after their 52-28 win over Ole Miss on Saturday. Florida's rushing attack looks absolutely phenomenal and Ole Miss was helpless to stop it. Jadan Baugh has already rushed for 11 touchdowns as he had 29 carries for 142 yards against the Rebels. With games against both Georgia and Texas in October, we'll get a good idea of where Florida stacks up after the Gators were picked ninth in the SEC's preseason media poll.

There's no need to write off any of these teams just yet. But they're also a tier behind the top four simply because they already have a conference loss. Ole Miss' win over LSU in Week 3 could be massive in the late-season tiebreaker race, and LSU worked out its frustrations on Saturday night in a blowout win over Texas A&M.

Tennessee's Faizon Brandon had his welcome-to-the-SEC moment against Texas, as he was just 17-of-29 passing for 145 yards and was constantly under pressure. Brandon should only get better, and Tennessee still has a path to a nine-win season.

The Bulldogs are 4-0 after a 31-24 win over the Tigers. Mississippi State squandered a 14-0 lead before outscoring the Tigers 14-0 in the fourth quarter to get the win. MSU has won its first four games of the season in back-to-back years for the first time since 1944 and 1945. But the Bulldogs finished last season at 5-8. We think it'll be a bit different this year with Kamario Taylor entrenched as the team's starting QB.

Kentucky's Week 3 win over Texas A&M was a statement and the Wildcats should be favored against South Carolina in Week 5. The big test comes in Week 6 against No. 10 LSU. Another win there and the Wildcats might be for real.

Auburn took down Vanderbilt on Saturday as Byrum Brown threw for a TD and ran for another. Both the Tigers and Commodores have daunting schedules going forward and might be reduced to playing spoiler sooner rather than later.

The playoff dream already looks very over

It's hard to see how either the Aggies or Sooners are going to be relevant in the playoff conversation now that both teams are 2-2. And it's not just about their records, either. A&M has now been soundly beaten in back-to-back weeks, and Oklahoma's offense can't get out of its own way. After beating UTEP 51-0 in Week 1, Oklahoma has scored six times and committed nine turnovers.

The only time the Gamecocks could be favored the rest of the season may come at Arkansas on Nov. 14. That's about as fitting a statement as you can make about these teams. After Kentucky visits in Week 5, South Carolina has Florida and Tennessee on the schedule.

Arkansas fans are already in a somber mood and a 34-6 win over Tulsa on Saturday wouldn't have done much to cheer them up. A win at Texas A&M next week would, however.

Boise State : The Broncos are now the clear favorites for the Group of Six spot in the playoff. Any chance Western Michigan had of capitalizing on its near-win against Michigan disappeared in a 32-7 defeat to the other Broncos. Boise State scored in every quarter and absolutely held the Western Michigan offense in check. WMU had just 223 yards and ended up averaging more yards per carry (5.1) than yards per pass attempt (3.8). Boise State QB Maddux Madsen was 16-of-23 passing for 204 yards and three touchdowns, while Dylan Riley rushed 28 times for 138 yards and a score. Assuming the American Conference doesn't produce a dominant team, Boise State could get into the playoff with two losses.

Wisconsin : The Badgers are now 3-1 after a 24-20 win over No. 13 Penn State . And an eight-win season suddenly looks very real. USC and Iowa are the only two ranked teams remaining on Wisconsin's schedule, and the Badgers' November slate includes Rutgers, Maryland , Purdue and Minnesota. Could 8-4 be enough to save Luke Fickell's job? It's very possible, especially after Saturday's win.

UCF : The Knights got a huge win to open Big 12 play. Without QB Alonza Barnett, UCF beat TCU 21-13 to move to 3-1 overall. Backup Keyone Jenkins threw one TD … and still had as many touchdowns as incomplete passes. Jenkins was 19-of-20 passing for 160 yards as Taevion Swint and Landen Chambers also rushed for a score.

Clemson: Hey, the Tigers are 3-1 and got a 24-10 win at Cal on Friday night. That's worthy of a mention. A cross-country trip is hard enough for a team even without one less day of rest. But Clemson committed to the ground game and ran the ball 49 times for 255 yards as Gideon Davidson carried the ball 22 times for 159 yards and two touchdowns. The defense held Cal to 231 total yards and picked off Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele twice.

Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker : The North Texas transfer threw for 389 yards and three scores as the Cowboys moved to 3-1 with a 41-24 win at West Virginia . Oklahoma State had 609 total yards as Caleb Hawkins had 31 carries for 180 yards and a score and Wyatt Young had eight catches for 192 yards and a TD. Guess what? Both of them followed coach Eric Morris from North Texas too.

Colorado : It's hard to see how Colorado's rebound happens in 2026. The Buffaloes lost 23-13 to Baylor a week after a 41-7 thrashing at Northwestern. That's 20 points over the last two games. And a big reason why Deion Sanders turned to Isaac Wilson . JuJu Lewis was 11-of-16 passing for just 75 yards before Wilson entered the game. Wilson finished 12-of-25 passing for 156 yards and a score. But that fourth-quarter touchdown came too late to make much of a difference. The Buffs have games against Texas Tech and Utah over the next three weeks. A 2-4 start is looking very likely.

No. 16 Louisville : Any control the Cardinals took in the ACC title game race after a Week 3 win over SMU disappeared with a 30-27 home loss to Wake Forest on Saturday. Louisville gave up 21 points in the second quarter and was shut out in the fourth thanks to a turnover on downs and two missed field goals. Louisville gained just 6 yards after taking over at the Wake Forest 44-yard line before failing on fourth down. And then Carson Hilbert missed a potential game-tying 42-yard field goal with 2:29 to go before Nick Keller's 57-yard attempt was blocked with 15 seconds remaining.

Maryland: The Terrapins had a bad, bad day at home against UCLA . After failing to score in the first quarter, UCLA still pasted Maryland 54-3. Malik Washington threw four interceptions and Kaleb Webb lost a fumble as hardly anything went right for Maryland. UCLA RB Wayne Knight III continued his touchdown party with 10 carries for 100 yards and a score as UCLA rushed 39 times for 266 yards and four touchdowns as a team. Unless things get better quickly, it's hard to see how Maryland doesn't explore moving on from Mike Locksley in 2027.

Anyone watching the end of Virginia Tech 's win over Boston College : The ACC Network broadcast of Virginia Tech's 21-14 win had technical difficulties thanks to a power issue around the Chestnut Hill area. That meant that viewers didn't see the final two minutes of the game, though at least no one scored. The last stretch of the game was simply Virginia Tech milking the clock for the win.

articles.title: Misery Index: Lincoln Riley, USC come up short yet again — and it's fair to ask how much more Trojans fans can bear
articles.summary: USC's defense was the root of its demise yet again — not even a dirty hit on Oregon QB Dante Moore could save the Trojans from another disappointing loss. An...
articles.body:
There comes a point in every failed coaching tenure when you have to ask the question: If not now, when?

Lincoln Riley is squarely in the middle of that conversation.

It is Year 5 at Southern Cal. He has been given everything he needs to win, from a massive contract to a well-funded roster to a palatial new football facility. He spent the offseason talking about having alignment with the administration and a roster capable of winning in the Big Ten.

He hired his third defensive coordinator in Gary Patterson, who happens to be one of the greatest defensive minds in the history of the sport. He has an experienced quarterback in senior Jayden Maiava . And on Saturday, he had Oregon at home playing without its starting quarterback for the entire second half.

When's it ever going to be enough for Riley at USC ? Or, more to the point, when is USC going to say it's had enough?

The evidence is in. USC fans don't need any more to render a verdict — and it is beyond a reasonable doubt.

USC's 41-27 loss to Oregon on Saturday was a moment of clarity because it exposed that for all the talk about what's different at USC, not much has really changed. Whether it's Caleb Williams or Jayden Maiava playing quarterback for Riley, it's the same product year after year after year.

And it's not good enough to win at the level Riley was hired to achieve.

There will be plenty of time to dissect why it's turned out this way and how both the Trojans and Riley can unwind themselves from this marriage. But when you knock out Oregon quarterback Dante Moore on a dirty hit and then celebrate it going to the sideline, as USC's Desman Stephens did before he got tossed from the game , there should be no excuse or tolerance for allowing 28 second-half points and 289 passing yards to backup Dylan Raiola .

It's even worse, though, that nobody's surprised. In fact, it's almost expected at this point because USC's big issues don't change from year to year.

It doesn't matter if it's Patterson or Alex Grinch or D'Anton Lynn, who have all had success elsewhere. You can even go back to Oklahoma , and it was the same problem. Season after season, Riley's teams have a brand — and that brand is needing a Heisman Trophy-winning college quarterback like Baker Mayfield or Kyler Murray to score on darn near every possession.

How do you win that way over the long haul? It doesn't work.

And the only common denominator is Riley.

While it's unreasonable to write off the season for a 4-1 team with this much talent, USC still has to play at Penn State , Wisconsin , Indiana and UCLA , with a home game against Ohio State . If the Trojans can get to the CFP for the first time under Riley with that schedule, we'll do all the mea culpas.

But the way they play football — remember, USC gave up 35 points to Rutgers last week! — does not lend itself to running the table. That's why the Oregon game feels like such a referendum on the Riley era. When you have that kind of opportunity at home and don't cash it with so much is riding on this season, it's the most disappointing moment of his tenure.

And that's why USC reigns as America's most miserable fan base in Week 4.

ACC: Four games into Tosh Lupoi's tenure at Cal, fans are starting to notice that their head coach is going through some growing pains. One example occurred at the end of the half Friday night in a 24-10 loss to Clemson, when Lupoi could have called a quick timeout after a sack and gotten the ball back with about 40 seconds on the clock. But Lupoi hesitated for about 15 seconds — he admitted his mistake after the game — and cost Cal a chance to make anything out of that possession. It probably wasn't the difference in winning or losing, but it is indicative of a guy who wasn't quite ready for all the things you deal with as a head coach. Here's the thing, though. Cal knew that — or at least, it should have. Lupoi, a former Cal player, got the job because his strength is recruiting. As a result, everything around him should be oriented to helping him as a tactician. That's where you have to question both Lupoi and general manager Ron Rivera for hiring 30-year-old Jordan Somerville to be the offensive coordinator. Somerville's previous job was three seasons as the assistant to Tampa Bay Bucs quarterback coach Thad Lewis . Even if you think Somerville is a future star in the profession, that's a big step up in responsibility and a weird fit alongside a first-time head coach. It also seems to have had a negative effect on promising quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele , who has not taken the expected leap as a sophomore. Lupoi needs to be insulated by experience or it could be a rough ride until he figures this head coaching thing out.

Big 12: A quick recap of Colorado 's 23-13 loss to Baylor would include several grisly details, including quarterback Julian Lewis getting benched, an offense that ran the ball 39 times for 2.1 yards per carry, getting stuffed three straight times from midfield in the second quarter and allowing four different punt returns of more than 15 yards. But none of that was quite as ridiculous as Deion Sanders' assessment of his team, which is now 2-2 after last week's stunning 41-7 loss at Northwestern. "We're better than this," Sanders said. "I know it's a tremendous letdown last week but we flushed it and we found out last night that team is better than you think. But we're better than this. It seems as though we're better than our opponents but the score just not dictating that. And that's the fascinating thing about it. We've got to find out why." If you're a Colorado fan, you have to be wondering what that even means. Colorado fans watched those games. What happened in either of them to suggest that Colorado is "better" than either Northwestern or Baylor? Better how? Are the players better? Is the coaching better? Or maybe the only thing that's actually better is the delusion about where Colorado's program is at right now. Even Colorado's big win in the season opener against Georgia Tech is looking less impressive now that we know Georgia Tech has clearly declined significantly from a year ago. With Colorado's toughest Big 12 home games against Texas Tech and Utah coming up in the next few weeks, this could get away from Sanders quickly and spark a fresh round of speculation about whether he's going to be there for the long haul.

SEC: Texas A&M made the College Football Playoff last season, and no one can take that away from them. But just 10 months later, this doesn't look like the same program. Was former offensive coordinator (now current Kansas State head coach) Collin Klein really that indispensable for quarterback Marcel Reed , who has struggled badly this year? Was demoting defensive coordinator Jay Bateman, causing him to leave for Kentucky , a gaffe by head coach Mike Elko? Or was Texas A&M's 11-0 start to last season a bit of a mirage, the product of arguably the easiest SEC schedule we may ever see in the College Football Playoff era? It's probably all of the above and then some, but what we know for sure is the wheels came off the wagon Saturday night in a 35-6 loss at LSU . If Elko was looking for his team to respond one week after a shocking home loss to Kentucky, it now heads home with all kinds of questions and its CFP hopes effectively over. Elko is somewhat protected by a six-year, $69 million contract extension that he signed last fall during the euphoria of the Aggies reaching No. 3 in the polls in mid-November. Then again, this is the same school that fired Jimbo Fisher with $77.5 million left on his contract. With oil trading at around $100 a barrel these days, don't eliminate any possibility if Texas A&M's biggest boosters are angry enough. Going back to the end of last season, the Aggies are 1-4 against their last five against FBS opponents. Individually, they are not necessarily awful losses. But the idea that A&M is an ascendent power under Elko, which made all the sense in the world midway through last season, now seems like a fantasy. In retrospect, four of A&M's seven SEC wins last season came against teams that fired their coaches. And that doesn't even include an improbable win over 4-8 South Carolina in which they trailed by 27 points at halftime. It all came together for Elko a year ago, but now it's coming undone.

Group of Six: As the season goes along, keep an eye on San Diego State . Sean Lewis, the head coach, is a bit of a media darling because he got the job at Kent State very young (he was 32 at the time), went 24-31 at a place that hadn't been very successful and left that job in 2023 to be the offensive coordinator at Colorado. When Coach Prime stripped his play-calling duties in November of that season, it was painted as unjust. Lewis, however, came out smelling like a rose when San Diego State hired him weeks later to be head coach. But now three years in, Lewis may have the most disappointing team in the Group of Six. Aztec fans are furious, and rightly so, after a 41-16 loss to Toledo. San Diego State now enters Pac-12 play at 1-3, having scored just 39 total points in its three losses to UCLA, James Madison and the Rockets. It may turn out that San Diego State has simply played a difficult schedule, as those opponents are a combined 11-1. But the new Pac-12 needs SDSU to be a premier program as it relaunches the league, and so far the Aztecs aren't holding up their end of the bargain.

Mike Locksley: It's all over but the buyout. Locksley has had plenty of time to get Maryland into a more competitive place in the Big Ten, but a 54-3 loss at home to UCLA in a stadium that emptied out early Saturday feels definitive. That doesn't necessarily mean Maryland will make the move right away, but you can't survive a 51-point loss to UCLA in Year 8 when you're already on the hot seat after consecutive 4-8 seasons. If anything, Locksley has gotten more rope than most coaches would because he is so well-connected as a recruiter in the mid-Atlantic and Maryland wanted to see if increasing investment in the roster rather than paying a big coaching buyout would make a difference. But, alas, consecutive home losses to Virginia Tech and UCLA — both with first-year coaches that would have been logical Maryland candidates had they fired Locksley last year — is pretty much the last straw for a fan base that can no longer make excuses for his 17-49 record in the Big Ten.

Brent Venables: The offensive dysfunction at Oklahoma is startling. In three games against power conference opponents, the Sooners have scored a mere 37 total points. And nearly a third of those came in the second half of Saturday's 41-13 loss to Georgia after the Bulldogs had throttled down with a big lead. While Oklahoma has a bye week to regroup, fans have every right to dread what's coming on Oct. 10 against Texas' loaded defense. How are the Sooners going to score on those guys? Funny things tend to happen in the Red River Rivalry, but if Oklahoma plays as badly in that game as it has the last two years against Texas (outscored by a combined 57-9), Venables — who just got a contract extension before the season — is going to be under pressure to make big changes. Offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle and quarterback John Mateer came to Oklahoma as a package deal from Washington State and looked like a dynamic combination early last season. But for whatever reason, Mateer seems to have regressed and everything looks really hard for this offense, whether they're playing a championship-level defense like Georgia's or a good Group of Six defense like New Mexico 's.

Curt Cignetti: We have gotten to the point with Indiana that when it survives a close call, as it did Friday night in a 29-23 win over Northwestern, the group chats start to get a little angsty and extra punctuation starts to show up in message board threads like "WHAT'S WRONG???????" This was, more or less, the Alabama football experience starting in about 2012 until Nick Saban retired, and every so often he'd have to scold the fan base back to reality. Cignetti is well aware of how this works because after the game, he got to the press conference and offered the following: "It's a good win cause you can lose those games very, very easily. I'm sure everybody's disappointed because they still have the national championship hangover but I can't do anything about that," he said, finishing the thought with a bit of an evil laugh as he chomped on a wad of gum. Cignetti is right, but once you give fans a taste of Michelin-star cooking, it's hard to go back to fast food.

Matt Campbell: In the fourth quarter of Penn State's 24-20 loss at home to Wisconsin, the Nittany Lions' offense had four consecutive three-and-outs and their defense gave up drives of 75 and 85 yards in the final seven minutes. Other than that, everything went great in Campbell's first Big Ten game. Honeymoon? What honeymoon? Campbell has an outstanding track record at Iowa State and Toledo, but he was something like Penn State's 12th choice for the job after its long coaching search went sideways last fall. Everyone knows that, which does not make things easy for him in earning the fan base's trust. A fourth-quarter collapse to a Wisconsin program that hadn't beaten a ranked team on the road since Oct. 30, 2021, will not help matters.

Dylan Stewart 's meltdown: A moment captured by TV cameras during South Carolina's 49-18 loss at Alabama should be concerning to Gamecocks fans. Stewart, their star defensive end, threw an obvious punch at Alabama tight end Josh Ford in the fourth quarter right in front of the referee that somehow didn't lead to his ejection. And earlier in the game, after a roughing-the-passer penalty, Stewart appeared to ignore coach Shane Beamer as the coach was was chewing him out coming to the sideline. Stewart has had an injury-plagued season, but South Carolina is a 2-2 team with a lot of problems on the field and potentially in the locker room.

Michigan 's regression to the mean: If Wolverines fans are being honest, they stole one they didn't deserve earlier this year against Western Michigan on a Hail Mary that the NCAA acknowledged never should have been allowed due to misapplied instant-replay protocols. When that kind of thing happens, karma is always waiting right around the corner. So perhaps the football gods are now even with Michigan after allowing an 11-play, 91-yard drive in just 106 seconds against Iowa, which won 20-19 on a touchdown pass as time expired.

ESPN's microphone mystery: In anticipation of President Donald Trump attending Texas-Tennessee, Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian said that it could be an issue for their headset communications if he were to go to the bathroom, for instance. Why? Because, according to Sarkisian, it happened at last year's national championship game, which Trump also attended. This led to a couple days' worth of stories exploring the issue. So it was an odd coincidence that when sideline reporter Laura Rutledge attempted to explain to the ESPN audience that the Secret Service can impact radio frequencies due to "electromagnetic deconfliction," the microphones being used by Chris Fowler and Kirk Herbstreit suddenly got overtaken with static. Though it likely had nothing to do with Trump, the timing couldn't have been more weird.

articles.title: Un derbi asturiano para despegar
articles.standfirst: Irregular inicio liguero de ambos • Calero llega con el ataque bajo mínimos • Larcamón quiere estrenarse con un triunfo gijonés que no llega desde 2001
articles.summary: Irregular inicio liguero de Oviedo y Sporting • Calero llega con el ataque bajo mínimos • Larcamón quiere estrenarse con un triunfo gijonés que no llega desde 2001
articles.body: La Segunda división recupera uno de los derbis más pasionales del fútbol español, como lo definió el debutante Nico Larcamón. Y es que un Oviedo que aún no ha ganado en el Tartiere este curso y un Sporting que ha vencido en sus dos salidas afrontan el derbi asturiano para dar un salto en la clasificación tras un inicio liguero irregular. Julián Calero afronta el duelo con varias ausencias de peso, especialmente en ataque. Isfan se ha quedado finalmente fuera de la convocatoria después de no ejercitarse el viernes y se suma a las bajas de Ilyas Chaira, Estanis Pedrola, Carlos Fernández y Brandon Domingues. Tampoco ha entrado Nacho Vidal, pese a que el lateral dio un paso adelante en su recuperación al iniciar la última sesión al ritmo de sus compañeros. Calero completa una lista de 20 futbolistas en la que aparecen los jóvenes Marco Esteban, Diego Menéndez y Enzo Pérez. Por su parte, Nicolás Larcamón quiere seguir en la senda de las victorias a domicilio y estrenarse por todo lo alto en un derbi que vuelve a jugarse casi dos años después y al que llegan ambos con la necesidad compartida de sumar un triunfo tras arrancar la Liga con más sombras que luces. Será el derbi número 119, con 50 triunfos del Oviedo, 36 del Sporting y un total de 32 igualadas... mientras que los rojiblancos no ganan un derbi en el estadio del Oviedo desde octubre de 2001 Así, el Sporting llega con la intención de volver a ganar en el Carlos Tartiere 25 años después. Una mala racha de un cuarto de siglo de duración que Larcamón quiere cortar para reengancharse a la parte noble de la clasificación. El técnico argentino no podrá contar con los lesionados Konrad de la Fuente, Bruno Rubio, Hugo Guillamón y Andrés Ferrari, mientras que recupera al capitán Gaspar Campos, que se reencontrará con Julián Calero, actual entrenador del Oviedo y su gran valedor en el Burgos. Un regreso vital para un Sporting que quiere volver a coronarse en una de las rivalidades más intensas del panorama nacional

articles.title: Rafa Márquez debuta como seleccionador de México con un empate contra Colombia
articles.standfirst: Luis Suárez y Gilberto Mora fueron los autores de los goles
articles.summary: Luis Suárez y Gilberto Mora fueron los autores de los goles
articles.body: Rafael Márquez debutó este sábado como seleccionador de México con un empate 1-1 contra la selección colombiana, que con este amistoso comenzó su nueva etapa sin James Rodríguez ni Juan Fernando Quintero. En el estadio M&T Bank Stadium de la ciudad estadounidense de Baltimore, los cafeteros tomaron la ventaja con una anotación de Luis Suárez, mientras que sus rivales igualaron con un tanto del juvenil Gilberto Mora. Justamente el Tri, liderado en la mitad de la cancha por Mora, de 17 años, se hizo del balón desde el comienzo y se ubicó en territorio colombiano para tratar de hacer daño. Sin embargo, los suramericanos fueron los que consiguieron abrir el marcador al minuto nueve en una gran jugada individual del volante Richard Ríos por el costado derecho, desde donde mandó un centro preciso para que el goleador Luis Suárez anticipara al defensor que lo marcaba y mandara el balón al fondo con un potente cabezazo. Los mexicanos retomaron el control de la pelota pero tuvieron muchas dificultades para romper la defensa, liderada por el capitán Dávinson Sánchez, muy correcto en la marca y en el uno contra uno. Las dos oportunidades claras de los dirigidos por Márquez llegaron al 32 en una gran jugada elaborada por Mora, en la que el extremo Roberto Alvarado sacó un remate cruzado que se estrelló en el palo derecho y en el rebote el centrocampista Luis Chávez disparó en el área y la pelota pegó en el horizontal. En la segunda parte, México salió con todo y tuvo la primera en un mano a mano, en el que Hirving 'Chucky' Lozano chutó y atajó el colombiano Álvaro Montero, aunque la jugada fue anulada luego por un fuera de lugar del atacante de Los Ángeles Galaxy. La selección cafetera respondió con un remate del centrocampista Jhon Arias, que se estrenó con la 10 del equipo, en un tiro libre que exigió al portero Rangel. El 1-1 de La Tri llegó al 62 cuando Jesús Gallardo filtró un pase largo para Mora, que apareció en el área, se deshizo con un enganche del central Jhon Lucumí y sacó un remate imposible de atajar para Montero. Con el paso de los minutos empezaron a llegar los cambios y tanto los mexicanos como los colombianos comenzaron a probar cosas nuevas. En el caso de los cafeteros, debutaron con la camiseta tricolor el lateral Samuel Velásquez, el centrocampista juvenil Matías Orozco, que milita en el Castellón español y el delantero Kevin Viveros, del Athletico Paranaense, quien es el máximo goleador del Brasileirao. En el equipo norteamericano, entre tanto, pescaron minutos el atacante Germán Berterame, el centrocampista Jeremy Márquez y el extremo Isaías Violante. Al final ninguno de los dos equipos fue profundo y el marcador no se movió más, por lo que Márquez no pudo debutar con una victoria, pero su equipo dejó buenas sensaciones, al igual que el dirigido por el argentino Néstor Lorenzo. Ficha técnica: 1. México: Raúl Rangel; Jorge Sánchez (m.74, Jeremy Márquez), Ismael Reyes, Johan Vásquez, Jesús Gallardo (m.63, Mateo Chávez); Erik Lira, Luis Chávez (m.63, Álvaro Fidalgo), Gilberto Mora (m.63, Obed Vargas); Roberto Alvarado (m.74, Isaías Violante), Hirving Lozano (m.63, Orbelin Pineda) y Armando González (m.74, Germán Berterame). Seleccionador: Rafael Márquez. 1. Colombia: Álvaro Montero; Daniel Muñoz, Davinson Sánchez, Jhon Lucumí, Álvaro Angulo (m.66, Álvaro Angulo); Gustavo Puerta, Kevin Castaño (m.71, Matías Orozco), Richard Ríos (m.71, Yaser Asprilla), Jhon Arias; Carlos Andrés Gómez (m.66, Jaminton Campaz) y Luis Suárez (m.66, Kevin Viveros). Seleccionador: Néstor Lorenzo. Goles: 0-1, m.9: Luis Suárez. 1-1, m.62: Gilberto Mora. Árbitro: el estadounidense Guido González. Amonestó a Luis Suárez, Álvaro Angulo, Hirving Lozano, Jorge Sánchez. Incidencias: Partido amistoso disputado en el M&T Bank Stadium de la ciudad estadounidense de Baltimore.

articles.title: Scotland: From turgid to thrusting - mixed start for new Scotland
articles.summary: BBC Sport Scotland's Tom English reviews a mixed start to life as Scotland head coach for Sebastien Pocognoli as his side open their Nations League campaign with a goalless draw in Slovenia.
articles.body:
For 45 turgid minutes in Slovenia, some in the Tartan Army might have reimagined the Steve Clarke years as a time of plenty, the halcyon era of ambitious football when Scotland were an all-electric thrill-fest.

The opening half of the Sebastien Pocognoli regime was, as expected, disjointed.

It was also, rather unexpectedly, devoid of anything remotely related to what Pocognoli laid out as his non-negotiables - front-foot pressing, high intensity, speed of thought and mind, goal threat.

They had no shot on target and lost so many aerial duels that you stopped counting beyond the half-hour mark. They took 38 minutes to touch the ball in Slovenia's penalty area.

It wasn't like they were under major pressure - the hosts are a pretty toothless side - but neither were they accurate or energetic. Everybody who preached patience in the new era gulped hard. This was not good. We didn't expect champagne, but this was stale beer.

And then it changed, not so completely that Scotland roared and won the game , but they certainly cleared their throats as an attacking force.

Gilmour catalyst, impressive Welsh, but same issue for Scotland?

Scotland begin Pocognoli era with encouraging Slovenia draw

McBurnie and co show promise without poise

From being impotent, they became thrusting. That second half was as big a 0-0 rout as you're likely to see. Frustrating, but encouraging at the same time.

It will be agonising for Oli McBurnie that he's still without an international goal - he said he wouldn't sleep after failing to convert a one-on-one with Jan Oblak - but his second-half performance was full of good things; efforts on goal, link-up play, presence and danger.

Robbie Ure hit a post, Kieron Bowie had a terrific chance, but missed. The three strikers drew a blank, but as far as 0-0s go, it offered hope that more productive days may lay ahead with these guys.

There are two ways of looking at the draw. All 10 starting outfield players had a shot on goal, the first time that's happened since June 2022, against Armenia.

Scotland had 17 shots, their most attempts in a competitive game in more than 14 years. The flipside is that they have now failed to score in three tournament games in a row for the first time in almost 22 years.

After the break, Pocognoli dropped McBurnie a little deeper, in a pocket just behind Robbie Ure and then Bowie when he came on. He got Billy Gilmour to sit lower in midfield, where he had time to dictate, which he absolutely did. Gilmour tied it all together in the second half.

Pocognoli called it "two games in one game" and he was right. The subtle shift in McBurnie's and Gilmour's positioning brought Scotland alive.

It was an impressive watch; ambition, relentlessness, belief. No cherry on top but enough there to leave most folk happy about day one and motivated ahead of day two, against Switzerland on Tuesday night at Hampden.

McBurnie, not so much the prodigal son but now the forgiven one, had that big chance six minutes into the new half - the one he would have dreamed about. He created it for himself, winning possession and getting into a wonderful position right in front of an isolated Oblak.

He could have dinked it as the goalkeeper committed himself, he could have slid it home to Oblak's left or through his legs. Instead, he went for the flourish, trying to take it round the Slovenian and marking his return to the side after 2,005 days in the wilderness with a first goal on his 17th appearance.

Oblak won the duel. Painful, for sure, but a prelude to a stirring second half from the striker and his new-old team-mates. McBurnie played a slick one-two with the increasingly dominant Gilmour, who had his shot saved. Oblak was by a million miles Slovenia's best player.

McBurnie had a header fly over, Aaron Hickey had a header just wide, Bowie came on and had an immediate impact. He had three chances in eight minutes - a tame shot, a clipped attempt and then the big one - played in by Gilmour but pulled wide. In that moment, he joined McBurnie and Ure (after hitting a post late in the first half) in the torture chamber.

In the midst of all of that, McBurnie powered a header on goal, but Oblak was equal to it. That was Scotland's ninth consecutive crack without reply. They were utterly dominant but achingly goalless. So much encouraging stuff and yet just one point to show for it when it really should have been three.

Pocognoli said he was heartened by that second half. Scotland fans should be buoyed by the new head coach recognising the problems in his team and then fixing them.

With such a small track record to feed off, the subject of his tactical acumen was always going to be an interesting one - the ownership of the second 45 minutes showed that he's no slouch in identifying and changing the things that need to be changed.

Going with McBurnie and Ure up front was something of a surprise, but it sent a signal out that Scotland are here to go on the offensive rather than just defend their way to decent outcomes.

That didn't materialise in the first half, but it clicked in the second. It's a touch surreal that, at the end of another game when Scotland failed to score, there is a lot to be hopeful about in the men who are there to supply the goals.

McBurnie, Ure and Bowie are an exciting trio. When others are fit, there's Che Adams, Lawrence Shankland, Tommy Conway and Ross Stewart. Young James Wilson will have his moment at some point. New blood has joined the old guard and things should be better when everything settles down.

For Pocognoli, the next test is the biggest one. Switzerland, ranked 14th in the world, are missing some serious operators, but they are brilliantly coached by Murat Yakin and they're settled and formidable.

Their whole is greater than the sum of their parts. This will be a fascinating examination of Pocognoli's prowess. Win on Tuesday night and it's lift-off time.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Why are Arsenal struggling to score goals?
articles.summary: Arsenal are already playing catch-up in the WSL title race because they are struggling to score goals. BBC Sport examines why.
articles.body:
Arsenal go into their Women's Super League game at Stamford Bridge knowing defeat by rivals Chelsea would be a damaging result just four weeks into the season.

It feels like an extreme assessment but the Gunners know all too well that if they fall behind early on, it is hard to catch up in the WSL title race.

Renee Slegers' side are already seven points behind leaders Manchester City, albeit with a game in hand, and it would be foolish to give them further breathing space.

Successive draws against Crystal Palace and Manchester United have dented Arsenal's start to the campaign.

Their slow starts have proven to be their undoing in previous campaigns as their search for another WSL title has gone on for seven years.

In that time, they have lifted the Women's Champions League and Women's Champions Cup, proving they have a squad capable of winning major trophies.

But it is the same story so far in 2026-27 as Arsenal's shooting boots have been missing and their lack of ruthlessness in front of goal has proven costly.

They face serial winners Chelsea on Sunday (16:30 BST) knowing they need to get over the line this time.

"If I look at the last two games, not turning that dominance into goals and wins, is something we have to look at," said Slegers.

"We believe in the quality of the squad and their ideas. We can create in a variety of ways. When that starts clicking, it will be really good.

"It really is about the details in the final third."

Fox makes 'easy decision' to sign three-year Arsenal deal

Unanswered questions for English teams as Women's Champions League returns

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Arsenal were tipped by many to win the WSL this season having invested in their squad in the transfer window.

Germany duo Lisa Baum and Selina Cerci boosted their attacking ranks, though England winger Beth Mead left to join Manchester City.

Slegers still has a wealth of options to choose from up front with Chloe Kelly, Olivia Smith, Alessia Russo, Stina Blackstenius and Caitlin Foord all available, as well as the anticipated return of Michelle Agyemang later in the season.

But despite an array of talent, Arsenal have struggled to score goals.

Across their first three WSL games they have had 56 shots and scored just twice.

They needed a 95th-minute equaliser to draw 1-1 with Manchester United and only beat HB Koge with a 93rd-minute penalty in the Champions League on Tuesday.

They had 70 touches in Crystal Palace's box and 79% possession but were held to a 0-0 draw by the newly promoted side two weeks ago.

"It's a combination of things. There's some details in decision-making and some details in the technical execution," said Slegers after their draw with United.

"It's also the ruthlessness in front of goal. I know the players want it. They want to execute for Arsenal.

"What kind of situations are we setting up? What spaces do we occupy in the box? What are the runs like, but also other moments in the game?

"Counter-attacking moments and set-pieces - those are also moments for us to be dangerous from so it's not only breaking down a low block."

Arsenal are creating chances so that is not the problem - but is there anything Slegers can do to change things?

The obvious question is why England's number nine, Russo, is not playing in that position.

Only Manchester City striker Khadija Shaw scored more goals in the WSL than Russo's 13 last season and she was second in European competition, behind Barcelona's Ewa Pajor.

But Slegers, who has often rotated Russo's position, has preferred her in the number 10 role at some point in all their WSL games so far this season.

It has not paid off for Russo, who is yet to get off the mark, despite attempting 11 shots, including 10 from inside the box.

In total, she has netted just three times in 507 minutes as an attacking midfielder, compared with the 21 she has scored in 2,913 minutes as a striker under Slegers.

Russo has created 1.42 chances per 90 minutes in the number 10 role, more than as a striker (1.27) but she has fewer shots and passes finishing in the final third, and fewer shots from inside the box.

Another striking statistic is that Russo and team-mate Blackstenius have never directly combined for a goal while the England forward has started in midfield.

Against Manchester United, as Arsenal trailed 1-0 and were pushing for an equaliser - which eventually came from full-back Smilla Holmberg - Russo continued to play in midfield.

When asked what Slegers' plan was, she said: "Basically, we were expecting to be spending a lot of time in their half.

"It was looking at how we could pose as much threat as possible in the box, hence why both Stina Blackstenius and Alessia Russo started.

"There was double threat in that position. We wanted to keep Alessia as high as possible on the pitch. We know she can do both roles really well for us.

"She's a fantastic number nine. Stina played her role. Selina Cerci also made her official debut. She has other threats, like her aerial play and instincts in the box.

"We have three [players who can play there] but the plan was to have two number nines in the box as much as possible for crosses."

articles.title: Liverpool ready to sign one of the fastest players in the Premier League
articles.summary: Liverpool are prepared to sign one of the fastest players in the Premier League. Speed is an area where the Reds have bolstered their ranks over the course o...
articles.body:
Liverpool are prepared to sign one of the fastest players in the Premier League.

Speed is an area where the Reds have bolstered their ranks over the course of the summer. The addition of Victor Munoz and then the signing of Bradley Barcola has given Liverpool's attack a new dynamism.

But there's always a need for more speed.

Liverpool are increasingly part of a physical Premier League and Andoni Iraola 's style of play is very much based on high intensity and pressing.

It requires players who are quick, and who are also capable of running behind opponents.

Which is why Liverpool will be in the market for more attackers in the coming transfer windows. Particularly on one side of the attack.

The Reds did have an ideal player lined up for that role. His name was Yan Diomande and Liverpool were prepared to go all in. But when Paris Saint Germain and Real Madrid come calling, their voices become too cajoling to reject.

Diomande has ended-up in Madrid, and Liverpool pivoted to sign the best available winger on the market who was Bradley Barcola.

The Reds plans therefore became to replace Salah with Barcola, but only temporarily. Long-term Liverpool are still on the market to sign a right-winger, or at least someone who prefers to play there more often.

Liverpool lining up move for one of the fastest in the Premier League

The Reds are reportedly interested in Kevin Schade according to Sky Sports . Brentford are reportedly interested in renewing Schade's contract.

However, Liverpool are believed to be ready to make a move with Arsenal also interested in Schade, who is one of the fastest players in the Premier League and once clocked a top speed of 36.3km/h.

Schade is someone who can play across the front line, and he has shown to be a threat in the Premier League. He is capable of playing as a right-winger, which is where he played a lot at Mainz and for the German national team.

Jurgen Klopp used him as a right-winger on his debut as a coach of the national team.

Como defender Jacobo Ramón has established himself as a quality center-back just after leaving Real Madrid for €2.5 million in the summer of 2025. Jacobo Ramón was one of Real Madrid's options for the fourth center-back spot this past summer, but the Spanish defender prioritized his current role with Como and ultimately decided to stay in the Serie A to keep polishing his game.

Real Madrid will keep monitoring Ramón's performances with Como and so will other clubs like Arsenal or Chelsea , who have been intrigued by the quality and potential he's displayed in recent months, per that same report.

articles.title: Joan Laporta looking to plant his own candidate for next Barcelona election to ensure stability
articles.summary: Joan Laporta’s second spell as Barcelona president will forever be tainted because of Lionel Messi’s departure in 2021.But barring Messi’s exit, Laporta has...
articles.body:
Joan Laporta's second spell as Barcelona president will forever be tainted because of Lionel Messi's departure in 2021.

But barring Messi's exit, Laporta has barely put a foot wrong and has played a critical role in ensuring relative financial stability at the club, all the while helping lead the Catalans back to dominance.

However, Laporta won't be eligible to run for the next Barcelona election, which is why the Spaniard is already hard at work trying to ensure the stability will remain even after his exit.

Laporta looking to plant his own candidate

Laporta has been central to Barcelona's success. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

According to Diario AS , Laporta is entering his final term as president with the clear objective of achieving financial and social stability, while also preparing a successor from within his own ranks.

On September 19, the Barcelona members' assembly confirmed the appointment of the final seven board members who will serve alongside Laporta until 2031.

With the statutes preventing him from running again, the president is determined to avoid the internal tensions and boardroom defections that marked the latter stages of his first spell.

Across his two presidencies, Laporta has worked with 47 different board members, 17 of whom left before the end of their term.

To that end, Laporta has recently incorporated five new managers into his project: Carme Hortala, Jaume Santiveri, Xavier Barniol, Carles Ayats and Jaume Nicolas.

Laporta is looking to unite his loyalists. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

This final term is viewed as pivotal for Barcelona's long-term future, with several major objectives to fulfil.

Chief among them is completing the Espai Barca project and the renovation of the Camp Nou , building a winning team with a bright future, and paying off the club's substantial debt.

Laporta will be keen to avoid the disruptions that plagued his first spell, when institutional crises and a 2008 vote of no confidence forced significant changes to his board.

His second term has proven far more stable, marked by shrewd decisions such as the appointment of Hansi Flick and the activation of economic levers to steady the finances.

The key now, though, is succession. A group of Laporta loyalists appears united, but a continuity candidate must emerge from within to carry on his work.

And it is there, in identifying and backing the right successor, that the potential for fresh dissension could arise.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappé injury update: Real Madrid expect two-week absence with knee issue
articles.summary: Real Madrid expect Kylian Mbappé to be sidelined for around two weeks after confirming he has suffered a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of his left...
articles.body:
Real Madrid expect Kylian Mbappé to be sidelined for around two weeks after confirming he has suffered a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of his left knee.

The diagnosis, confirmed by the club on Saturday, suggests the injury is not as bad as first feared. There is an outside chance of Mbappe featuring in Madrid's next La Liga fixture, the visit of Villarreal on October 10.

The France captain was hurt on Friday during his country's 1-0 Nations League win over Türkiye, Zinedine Zidane's first match in charge. Mbappé scored the only goal early in the second half for France , but he sat on the turf rubbing his left knee moments later.

Zidane was downbeat on the forward's prognosis straight after the game.

"No, it's not good. It's not good, unfortunately. He will have to go back. We will not take risks, he has extended his knee when he took the shot. It's not very encouraging."

The French Football Federation said Mbappé had "suffered a tendon injury and will miss the rest of the camp", and he returned to Spain for a scan. France still face Belgium home and away and Italy in this window without their skipper.

Mbappé has been Madrid's top scorer again this season, with eight goals and two assists in eight games across all competitions, and he is on the 30-man shortlist for the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

Los Blancos will hope Mbappe can recover in time for their La Liga return next month. Jose Mourinho's side have made a mixed start to the league campaign with five wins and two defeats from seven fixtures. It leaves them six points behind Barcelona , who have made a perfect start to the campaign.

Madrid's injury list is also growing. Ibrahima Konate is out for around three to four weeks after getting hurt in the France camp, while Fede Valverde suffered a "grade three" ankle sprain in the derby defeat to Atletico Madrid that is expected to keep him out for weeks.

articles.title: Arsenal and Liverpool set to fail in move for La Liga star
articles.summary: Trent Alexander-Arnold, Arsenal and Real Madrid: January Move Unlikely as Right-Back Situation EmergesArsenal’s search for a right-back has led them towards...
articles.body:
Trent Alexander-Arnold , Arsenal and Real Madrid : January Move Unlikely as Right-Back Situation Emerges

Arsenal's search for a right-back has led them towards one of the most recognisable names on the market, at least in exploratory terms. According to TEAMtalk, Trent Alexander-Arnold has been discussed internally and via intermediaries as Premier League clubs assess whether there is any route to a deal from Real Madrid.

The current picture, though, is far calmer than the noise around it. Despite contact being made with Arsenal, Liverpool , Manchester City and Chelsea , the player is not actively looking to leave Madrid and a January transfer is not presently expected. That is the key detail in all of this, and it shapes the entire situation.

Arsenal monitoring Trent Alexander-Arnold position

Arsenal are understood to be among the clubs approached as part of checks on Alexander-Arnold's market. That makes obvious sense. He is 27, highly experienced, proven at elite level and operating in a position where top clubs are constantly alert to opportunity.

From an Arsenal perspective, this feels more like intelligent market awareness than a move advancing towards negotiation. Clubs at that level rarely ignore information on players of this calibre, particularly when their circumstances appear fluid. Real Madrid's recruitment of Denzel Dumfries has naturally altered the conversation around Alexander-Arnold's role, especially after he made more than 20 starts in his first season in Spain following his 2025 departure from Liverpool.

There is also the England angle. Missing out on Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad raised questions around his standing, even if his subsequent recall underlined that his quality remains respected. For interested clubs, that blend of pedigree and possible availability will always command attention.

Real Madrid stance shaping January transfer plans

For now, the decisive factor is the player's own outlook and Madrid's lack of intention to sanction a mid-season departure. Alexander-Arnold is not contemplating an exit at this stage, and there is no sign of an active effort to force one. Sources indicate the matter may be revisited after the season if circumstances change, but that is very different from a move gathering pace for January.

That distinction matters. Exploratory contact happens constantly at the top end of the game. Intermediaries sounding out clubs does not automatically mean a transfer is developing. In this case, it appears more accurate to describe the situation as one being watched closely rather than one moving towards resolution.

Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea all being alerted to the same opportunity says plenty about the regard in which Alexander-Arnold is still held. It also reflects the scarcity of top-level right-backs in the market. When one potentially becomes available, even hypothetically, the leading clubs take notice.

For Arsenal, this is a name worth tracking, no more and no less at present. Unless the player's stance shifts or Real Madrid reassess, the expectation remains that he stays where he is through January. The more realistic point for any meaningful decision, if one arrives, looks likely to be the end of the campaign.

From an intrigued Arsenal supporter's perspective, this is exactly the kind of report that grabs attention, even if it comes with a heavy dose of caution. Trent Alexander-Arnold is a huge name, a player with elite-level experience, creative quality and the sort of passing range that could add something different to any side.

The obvious attraction is that Arsenal are always looking for marginal gains, and bringing in a right-back of that profile would count as a major one. If there is any uncertainty over his standing at Real Madrid, of course Arsenal should be aware of it. That is what well-run clubs do.

At the same time, this does not read like a move that is close. It sounds more like groundwork, information gathering and seeing whether a future opening could appear. Supporters should probably resist getting carried away by the glamour of the name alone.

There would also be tactical questions. Alexander-Arnold offers immense quality on the ball, but Arsenal would need to be certain the overall balance works, especially in the biggest games. Still, if the chance ever became genuine, it would be hard not to be excited. Players of this calibre do not come onto the market often, and Arsenal being in that conversation says plenty about where the club now stands.

articles.title: Rui Pinto, el hacker que destapó la polémica del Manchester City, menciona a Guardiola
articles.standfirst: El pirata informático portugués fue quien filtró los millones de documentos confidenciales que desembocaron en el histórico expediente financiero contra el club inglés
articles.summary: El pirata informático portugués fue quien filtró los millones de documentos confidenciales que desembocaron en el histórico expediente financiero contra el club inglés
articles.body: Rui Pinto, un joven portugués apasionado de la informática y antiguo estudiante de Historia, pasó de ser un completo desconocido a convertirse en una de las figuras más controvertidas e influyentes del fútbol mundial. En 2015 creó la plataforma Football Leaks con la premisa de actuar como un informante para exponer las irregularidades operativas y contables del deporte de élite. Detrás del seudónimo "John", logró acceder sin autorización a los sistemas de diversos clubes, agencias de representación y estamentos deportivos de Europa, acumulando millones de archivos con correos, contratos secretos y transferencias opacas. El punto de inflexión del escándalo llegó en 2018, cuando filtró una masiva masa documental a la revista alemana Der Spiegel. Las revelaciones detallaban presuntas maniobras del Manchester City para eludir las normativas del Fair Play Financiero de la UEFA, inflando supuestamente los contratos de patrocinio procedentes de Emiratos Árabes Unidos y ocultando pagos paralelos a entrenadores y futbolistas. Estos archivos fueron el germen que impulsó la posterior investigación formal de la Premier League, que terminó formulando 115 cargos por infracciones financieras contra la entidad de Mánchester. El recorrido judicial de Pinto ha estado lleno de contrastes y batallas legales. En 2019 fue detenido en Budapest y extraditado a Portugal, donde afrontó acusaciones de acceso ilícito a datos, violación de correspondencia y tentativa de extorsión a un fondo de inversión. Tras ser condenado en 2023 a cuatro años de prisión en libertad condicional, pasó a colaborar activamente con las autoridades francesas y portuguesas, entregando discos duros cifrados adicionales y entrando en un programa de protección de testigos tras ser absuelto recientemente de cientos de cargos adicionales. Hoy en día, el legado de Rui Pinto divide por completo a la opinión pública y al entorno futbolístico. Para sus defensores y plataformas anticorrupción, se trata de un héroe de la transparencia cuyas filtraciones obligaron a fiscalizar el poder económico en el deporte rey. La ministra británica de Cultura y Deporte, Lisa Nandy, subrayó en El Corriere della Sera la necesidad de cerrar rápidamente el caso: "Hay que llegar a una conclusión rápida para restablecer la confianza en el fútbol. La Premier League tiene derecho a autogobernarse, pero las reglas deben aplicarse y ser respetadas por todos". Por su parte, Rui Pinto, también en declaraciones al mismo diario italiano, manifestó: "Una decisión histórica para el fútbol inglés, y una que corona el trabajo que he realizado a través de Football Leaks. Hoy, todos sabemos que, mediante manipulaciones estructurales y maniobras financieras, el Manchester City no simplemente eludió las reglas, las convirtió en una mera formalidad, desafiando cualquier intento de preservar la integridad de la competición. Ese fraude meticulosamente orquestado quedará finalmente sujeto a castigo, y el impacto no será solo turbulento, sino devastador... No puedo evitar recordar las palabras de Pep Guardiola en su primera rueda de prensa como entrenador del City: "Abróchense los cinturones de seguridad".
